note: Closed variety of the things the factory can test on: how each is driven and how its stand is checked. Read only by scripts/surfaces.py. A value a project can bring that this table lacks is a hint to a role, never a refusal (AR-2). The commands and patterns of a row are labelled by what was read: the Android device row and the Appium server row follow a real project's tooling read at a recorded revision (docs/tasks/specs/reports/t-524-ep1-41a-report.md); the iOS row and the W3C element and snapshot paths are general knowledge, not read from a real tool, and no row has run on a device (FR-33).

words.unknown_word: This project declares a test surface called "{word}" that the factory has no way to drive: those cases go to a person. If it is a kind of surface the factory should know, record it as a finding.
words.no_stand: This project runs native-application tests, but no stand for an agent's hands is described: those cases go to a person. Describe the device stand by running the onboarding again.

cli.words: Agent checks on a command-line application are not supported: those cases go to a person.

desktop.words: Agent checks on a desktop application are not supported: those cases go to a person.

artifact.note: The file the device holds, to tell a rebuild with the same version (EP1-41e). The two command forms (`pm path`, `sha256sum`) were read at the recorded revision (t-524-ep1-41a-report.md row [3]); the two patterns and the several `package:` lines of a split install are general knowledge, not read from a real tool.

ios.words: iOS: only a booted simulator is read (simctl), no real device is promised; this road has not been run on a real project.
